title: Meta made its own AI detection system. It should have just used Google’s
slides: Meta built an AI detector from scratch. Why not use Google’s?
Google’s SynthID already works for text and images
Meta’s version flags content Google misses — and some it doesn’t
You now face two incompatible detection standards across platforms
Pick one detector today and test it on your own content
thread_text:
1. Two detectors, one mess

Meta built its own AI detector from scratch instead of licensing Google’s SynthID.

2. Google’s tool has limits

SynthID already detects AI in text and images, but Meta claims it misses certain content.

3. Meta catches what Google misses

Meta’s version flags content Google overlooks, though some false positives remain.

4. Incompatible standards ahead

You now face two conflicting detection systems across platforms with no single answer.

5. Test one detector this week

Take a piece of AI-generated text and run it through either Meta’s or Google’s tool today.

instagram.caption:
Meta built its own AI detector from scratch, skipping Google’s ready-to-use SynthID tool.

Google’s system already works for images and text. Meta says it misses some AI content — but its own version tags false positives. You now have two incompatible detection standards across platforms.

If you create or publish content, there’s no single reliable check. A post flagged on one platform might pass the other.

Try this: drop a piece of AI text into Google’s tool today — will your own work survive the double test 🤖🔍
